title: A Clinical Trial With SENS-601, Injected With SPHYNX Administration System, in the Pediatric Population Presenting With Hearing Loss Related to Pathogenic Variation(s) of GJB2 Gene.
official: An Open-Label, Multicenter Phase 1/2 Study to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of Intracochlear Ascending Dose Injections of SENS-601 Followed by Expansion Cohort in Pediatric Population With Hearing Loss Related to Biallelic Pathogenic Variation(s) of GJB2, As Well As to Demonstrate the Performance of the Administration System, Its Safety, Its Clinical Benefit, and Its Usability.
summary:
Main objective: Part 1: assess the safety and tolerability of SENS-601, the SPHYNX administration system following unilateral injection of SENS-601 into the cochlea using the SPHYNX injection system.

Part 2: assess the efficacy of SENS-601 following bilateral intracochlear injection.
conditions: Hearing Loss Related to biallelic pathogenic variation (s) of the GJB2 Gene.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Are males or females aged ≥6 months to ≤6 years (corrected age in case of premature birth) at the time of SENS-601 administration.
2. 2. Have a diagnosis of congenital bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss.
3. 3. The participant’s legally authorized representative (LAR) must have given written informed consent and any authorization as required per local law and be able to comply with all study requirements.
4. 4. Have biallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic GJB2 variation(s), confirmed by DNA sequencing.
5. 5. Have a documented normal cochlea and internal auditory canals.
6. 6. Are affiliated with or is a beneficiary of a health care system.
7. 7. Have eligibility confirmed by the Principal Investigator after a local multidisciplinary evaluation.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Have a history of chronic, acute, or major disease.
2. 10. Have documented other causes of congenital bilateral hearing loss linked to mutations in genes other than GJB2.
3. 11. Require vaccination with a live attenuated vaccine from Screening up to 3 months following SENS-601 administration
4. 12. Are participating in any other interventional clinical study.
5. 13. Have any other condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, may compromise the safety or compliance of the participant or would preclude the participant from successful completion of the study or might interfere with the evaluation of study treatment.
6. 14. Are anticipated to be noncompliant with the Protocol requirements, in the opinion of the Investigator.
7. 15. Have a history of documented allergic reactions or acute hypersensitivity reactions attributed to SENS-601 excipients or impurities or SPHYNX components or any other medications used in this study.
8. 2. Plan to use other investigational drugs or has used other investigational drugs within 5 half-lives of SENS-601 administration, or until the expected pharmacodynamic effect has returned to baseline or enrolled in a clinical study with an investigational drug within the last 12 weeks, whichever is longer.
9. 3. Have been dosed in a previous gene therapy clinical study.
10. 4. Have hearing loss caused by developmental disorders (eg, cochlear aplasia or hypoplasia) or other diseases or risk factors.
11. 5. Have a prior or current cochlear implant in the ear to be treated with SENS-601.
12. 6. Have hearing loss due to any other cause that would impact negatively the response of hair cell function.
13. 7. Have other causes of hearing loss, such as unilateral hearing loss, chronic conductive hearing loss, malformation syndrome, or syndromic hearing loss.
14. 8. Have a contraindication to corticosteroid therapy and/or immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory therapy.
15. 9. Have a contraindication to the planned surgery, a contraindication to anesthesia or increased anesthesiologic risk, or a history of therapy known as ototoxic for an extended period.
